RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-99CC30886D-55239
Member: Morgan Carter (ID W450765041)
Requested service: Lumbar fusion, CPT 22612
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-07
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-03

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22612 (lumbar spinal fusion), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07, reference number POC-99CC30886D-55239. This appeal is timely, as it is submitted well before the stated deadline of 2027-02-03.

**1. The stated reason for denial does not match the record.**

The notice states that the request is denied because "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." The notice does not identify which records were considered or which specific items were missing, and it does not name or cite the specific medical policy or clinical guideline number applied to this determination. I am requesting, as part of this appeal, that the plan identify the specific guideline document (title, number, and version/date) that was applied to my case, and specify precisely what documentation was deemed missing, since — as detailed below — a complete clinical package supporting medical necessity was available at the time of the request.

The following documentation, summarized below, is enclosed with this appeal and should be considered part of the complete record:

- Symptom history: 12 months of progressive lower back and bilateral leg pain, unrelieved by rest.
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting a supervised course of physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), 10 weeks, 2026-04-15 through 2026-06-24, 24 visits completed.
- Medication trial records: NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-10 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- Imaging report dated 2026-06-23: MRI of the lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiographs showing grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension views, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.
- Functional assessment: inability to stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force cessation of activity, relieved by sitting (neurogenic claudication).
- Physical exam findings: neurogenic claudication; diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes; no bowel or bladder dysfunction; BMI 29; non-smoker; no active infection; no untreated substance use.
- Surgical consultation note from Dr. Okafor, MD (orthopedic surgery), recommending single-level fusion at L4-L5.

**2. The applicable medical-necessity criteria.**

My research, and Harvard Pilgrim's own published Musculoskeletal (MSK) Care Management Program materials, indicate that prior authorization review for lumbar spine fusion is performed by Harvard Pilgrim's vendor, Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates, Inc.), under "Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery." I was able to obtain and review the text of that guideline as published with an implementation date of July 2025; I have not been able to independently confirm that the wording is identical in the edition implemented in July 2026, which may be the version actually in effect on the date of this denial. I am requesting that Harvard Pilgrim confirm which edition of Guideline 1766 was applied and provide its exact text if it differs from what is quoted below.

The July 2025 edition of Guideline 1766 states, under its general statement:

"Operative treatment is indicated when the natural history of surgically treated lesions is better than the natural history for non-operatively treated lesions. All operative interventions must be based on a positive correlation with clinical findings, the natural history of the disease, the clinical course, and diagnostic tests or imaging results."

For single-level lumbar fusion, the guideline sets out the following surgical indications, which I address point by point against my clinical record:

- "Lumbar back pain, neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain ... that impairs daily activities for at least 6 months" — My symptoms have been present for 12 months (exceeding the minimum), with documented neurogenic claudication that limits standing/walking to under 10 minutes, clearly impairing daily activities. (I note the guideline text I retrieved qualifies this pathway as being "without sensory or motor deficit"; my exam shows diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes but no motor deficit and no bowel/bladder dysfunction. I ask the reviewer to apply clinical judgment as to whether this finding is consistent with radiculopathy under this pathway, since I am not aware of, and am not asserting, any plan text that further defines how sensory findings are treated under this criterion.)

- "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months" — I completed 10 weeks (24 visits) of supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-15 to 2026-06-24, well in excess of the required 6 weeks, in addition to 6 months of NSAID therapy and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-10 that provided only 2 weeks of partial relief. Per the guideline's own definition, "Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: ... Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment ..." — my continued, unrelieved symptoms after this full course of therapy and medication management satisfy this definition.

- "Imaging studies corresponding to the clinical findings" — The 2026-06-23 MRI and flexion-extension radiographs directly correspond to my clinical presentation, showing grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis and severe central stenosis at the same level (L4-L5) implicated by my exam and claudication pattern.

- "At least ONE of the following clinical conditions: ... Spondylolisthesis (neural arch defect - spondylolytic spondylolisthesis, degenerative spondylolisthesis, and congenital unilateral neural arch hypoplasia) ... Evidence of segmental instability - Excessive motion, as in degenerative spondylolisthesis, segmental instability, and surgically induced segmental [instability]" — My imaging documents grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, satisfying the spondylolisthesis criterion by name. It also documents 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension imaging, which I believe is objective evidence of the "excessive motion"/segmental instability referenced in this same criterion, though the guideline text I was able to retrieve was cut off before stating the plan's specific numeric threshold for "excessive motion." I am not asserting a specific millimeter or degree threshold on the plan's behalf; I am asking the reviewer to apply the plan's own internal threshold to the documented 5 mm of translation and to disclose that threshold to me if it is not met, so that I can respond further.

**3. Requested action.**

Based on the above, I ask that Harvard Pilgrim and/or Evolent:

1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22612 as requested by Dr. Okafor; or
2. If the plan still finds the record incomplete, specify exactly what additional documentation is required, given that PT records, medication trial history, MRI, flexion-extension radiographs, and a documented physical exam are all already part of the file; and
3. Provide me and my provider with the complete, currently-effective text of the specific guideline applied to CPT 22612 (title, guideline number, and effective/revision date), consistent with my right to know the criteria relied upon in this determination.

I am also requesting a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Okafor and the plan's reviewing physician, if that has not already occurred, to discuss the clinical findings summarized above.

I understand that if this internal appeal is denied, I have the right to request an external review through the Maine Bureau of Insurance within 12 months of the final adverse benefit determination, and I reserve that right.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if any additional information is needed to process this appeal. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Morgan Carter

Enclosures:
- Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-04-15 to 2026-06-24)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-04-10)
- MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiograph report, 2026-06-23
- Clinical exam notes documenting neurogenic claudication and L5 dermatomal findings
- Surgical consultation/letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, MD
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07 (Reference POC-99CC30886D-55239)
